newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom does not confirm asset seizure.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom does not confirm asset seizure.

text.p: Russia's RAO Gazprom, the world's biggest gas company, said on Tuesday it could not confirm that any assets of its subsidiaries had been frozen.

"RAO Gazprom does not confirm the fact that at the present time assets or property of the subsidiaries of RAO Gazprom, including Permtransgaz, Urengoigazprom, Yugtransgaz and Gazprom enterprises in the Komi Republic have been frozen," deputy chairman Vyacheslav Sheremet said in a statement issued to Reuters.
A spokesman declined to comment on the statement, and it was not clear whether Gazprom was denying its assets had been seized or frozen.

Last week Gazprom chairman Rem Vyakhirev wrote to deputies complaining that the accounts of several of Gazprom's subsidiaries, including Urengoigazprom, Uraltransgaz and Yugtransgaz, had been frozen, and assets were being inventoried for a possible auction.
He said the authorities were putting pressure on Gazprom to pay off tax arrears, but Gazprom itself was owed three times as much as it owed, with the government among its debtors.
Urengoigazprom accounted for nearly half of Gazprom's 1995 output.
On Monday Prime-Tass news agency said accounts at two Gazprom subsidiaries in Perm and the Komi Republic had been frozen.
The letter and reports have coincided with the launch of Gazprom's international share placement.
A Gazprom spokesman said on Monday that Vyakhirev's letter to deputies should not be taken literally and its main aim was to get Gazprom debtors to pay up.
